summary: Use a Badge to make a short status, category, or count easy to scan beside the content it describes.

useWhen.text: Show a short status, category or count beside the content it describes, so people can scan it.

from.quote: Use a Badge to make a short status, category, or count easy to scan beside the content it describes.

avoidWhen.text: The message needs a sentence or an explanation: keep the explanation out of the Badge.

from.quote: Avoid putting the whole explanation inside the Badge.

anatomy.holds: Optional leading node, such as an icon, that adds a recognizable cue without replacing the words.

from.quote: Adds a recognizable cue without replacing the words.

anatomy.holds: The label text; names the status or category.

from.quote: Names the status or category.

anatomy.holds: The token-owned surface that groups the message into one compact shape.

from.quote: Groups the message into one compact shape.

placementAdvice.text: Place the Badge next to the item it describes.

from.quote: Place the compact status next to the item it describes.

configuration.text: Use the solid treatment (type default) beside ordinary content.

from.quote: Use a solid Badge beside ordinary content.

configuration.text: Use type glass where the underlying image or surface stays part of the composition.

from.quote: Use glass where the underlying image or surface remains part of the composition.

configuration.text: Choose Badge Size for the density of the surrounding content.

from.quote: Choose the size for the surrounding density.

configuration.text: Choose a Semantic Intent and appearance whose meaning agrees with the status.

from.quote: Use semantic treatment that agrees with the status.

configuration.text: Give the status that needs attention the strongest Emphasis, rather than equal emphasis on every badge.

from.quote: Give the status needing attention the strongest emphasis.

configuration.text: Add onPress only when opening related detail is useful; most badges only inform.

from.quote: Add an action only when opening related detail is useful.

configuration.text: Pass the Badge's own modes object to the Icon in leading, with the Context4 that matches the treatment (solid or glass): Badge renders the leading node as given.

from.quote: It renders a supplied leading node verbatim, so the guide passes the same owner mode object to the public Icon and selects the matching `Context4` for Solid or Glass.

rules.text: Say one thing in a few words.

from.quote: Say one thing, in a few words.

rules.text: Write the status, not a sentence.

from.quote: Write the status, not a sentence
Use familiar words.

rules.text: Keep tense and capitalization consistent across a set of badges.

from.quote: Keep tense and capitalization consistent across the same set.

rules.text: Keep comparable statuses similar in length and capitalization.

from.quote: Keep comparable statuses similar in length and capitalization.

rules.text: Keep the label short so the Badge stays a compact companion; its width follows the label.

from.quote: Keep the label short so the Badge remains a compact companion.

rules.text: Let the label carry the meaning, and use emphasis to set priority.

from.quote: Let the label carry the meaning and use emphasis to establish priority.

states.when: Without onPress; most badges only communicate information.

from.quote: Most badges communicate information.

states.when: With onPress, when opening related detail is useful.

from.quote: Add an action only when opening related detail is useful.

states.when: loading is true while the value is still arriving.

from.quote: Loading shows that the value is still arriving.

accessibility.text: Rely on the visible label for an interactive Badge's accessible name, and verify that name: Badge ignores accessibilityLabel.

from.quote: The package currently ignores the supplied accessibilityLabel on Badge; rely on visible text and verify the resulting accessible name for an action.

doDont.dont: Avoid a sentence inside the Badge
doDont.why: Avoid putting the whole explanation inside the Badge.

from.quote: Use a short status

doDont.why: Conflicting words and tone make the status harder to trust.

from.quote: Match meaning and tone

doDont.why: If every status competes, the urgent one is harder to find.

from.quote: Reserve strong emphasis

doDont.why: Mixed wording and capitalization slow scanning.

from.quote: Use a consistent vocabulary

examples.purpose: A system status beside the item it describes, in a slim Card row.
examples.jsx:
<Card variant="slim" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <HStack alignVertical="center" justifyHorizontal="space-between" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
    <Text>September payment</Text>
    <Badge label="Paid" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Semantic Intent': 'System', AppearanceSystem: 'positive' }} />
  </HStack>
</Card>

from.quote: Place the compact status next to the item it describes.

examples.purpose: A solid badge with a leading icon; the Icon gets the Badge's modes, with Context4 Badge.
examples.jsx:
<Badge
  label="Paid"
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Badge Size': 'Medium', Context4: 'Badge' }}
  leading={<Icon iconName="ic_card" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Badge Size': 'Medium', Context4: 'Badge' }} />}
/>

from.quote: It renders a supplied leading node verbatim, so the guide passes the same owner mode object to the public Icon and selects the matching `Context4` for Solid or Glass.

examples.purpose: A badge that opens related detail.

from.quote: Add an action only when opening related detail is useful.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label text shown inside the badge. Default "Label", from the component source.

props.name: type
props.description: Visual style (matches the Figma `type` property). `'default'` is a solid token-colored pill; `'glass'` is a frosted, translucent pill backed by a real background blur (`GlassFill`) — the same glass surface used at the bottom of media/merchandising cards. Default "default", from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes used to resolve design tokens (e.g. Appearance, Size)

props.name: onPress
props.description: Optional press handler to make the badge interactive.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Ignored: the rendered wrapper does not get it.

props.name: leading
props.description: Rendered verbatim: Badge does not pass its modes to the leading node. Declared: Optional leading node (icon/image) rendered before the label, inside the badge surface. When present, the badge lays its contents out in a row.

props.name: glassOverlayColor
props.description: Glass-only override for the translucent overlay color painted over the live blur. Defaults to the `badge/glass/color/background` token. Ignored for the `'default'` type.

props.name: glassIntensity
props.description: Glass-only override for the blur intensity on the 0–100 scale. Defaults to the `blur/minimal` token. Ignored for the `'default'` type.

props.name: loading
props.description: Explicit per-instance loading override. When `true`, renders a badge-shaped skeleton placeholder instead of the badge. Defaults to inheriting from the surrounding `<SkeletonGroup>`.

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

props.name: ...Omit<React.ComponentProps<typeof View>, 'style' | 'accessibilityLabel' | 'accessibilityRole'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: AppearanceBrand
modes.description: A token collection Badge reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Context4
modes.description: The solid Figma master owns Context4=Badge. The package lists Badge/glass for the glass treatment, but the glass master's mode could not be resolved, so full mode parity is unverified.
